thread:
mira: Anyone seeing increased 5xxs from ap-northeast-1 edge pool? mount-proxy readiness failing since ~03:12 UTC, ALB healthchecks 504
joel: I rolled out edge-nacl-tightening-2026-03-17 last night — targeted a couple of subnets in ap-northeast-1 to clamp down ephemeral ranges
ashley: saw alerts too, spike in pod restarts and readiness failures. tcpdump from an affected node shows SYNs from ALB but no SYN-ACK back
infra-bot: config-change detected: user=joel change=edge-nacl-tightening-2026-03-17 targets=[subnet-0f2e3d] type=nacl-update ts=1950001240
mira: can you paste the NACL rules you applied? suspect asymmetric NACL deny on high ports
joel: pasted below (redacted):
```
Rule 100 ALLOW 0.0.0.0/0 TCP 80
Rule 110 DENY 10.0.0.0/8 TCP 1024-65535
Rule 120 ALLOW 0.0.0.0/0 ALL ICMP
```
ashley: that DENY on 10.0.0.0/8 is huge — our internal ELBs live in 10.0.0.0/8 in this VPC. NACLs are stateless so return high-port traffic gets blocked
mira: confirmed: ALB -> node SYN reaches, node SYN-ACK sent but NACL drops it on egress. healthchecks timed out at ALB -> 504s
joel: omg, I scoped it too broadly trying to prevent lateral nodeport probes. I'll revert the DENY immediately
mira: quick mitigation options: 1) add explicit ALLOW for the ALB CIDR on ephemeral ports 2) remove the DENY and rely on SGs for stateful intra-VPC restrictions 3) add symmetric allow rules for ephemeral ranges
ops-bot: runbook: https://intranet.redwood/procedures/nacl-change-checklist — validate ELB/ALB source ranges before changes
infra-bot: action=rollback user=joel change=edge-nacl-tightening-2026-03-17 rule_removed=110 subnet=subnet-0f2e3d ts=1950001301
joel: rollback applied, please verify health across AZs
ashley: running quick curl checks: curl -I http://mount-proxy.internal/health -> 200 OK from az-a, az-b, az-c :thumbsup:
mira: tcpdump now shows SYN->SYN-ACK flows; backend error rates dropping back to baseline
joel: follow-up: I'll open a ticket to refine the ACL change template and add automated ALB source CIDR validation, and avoid blanket 10.0.0.0/8 denies. Also documenting prefer SG-based controls for intra-VPC traffic
ops-bot: incident created INC-2026-1245 -> https://issues.redwood/INC-2026-1245
ashley: lesson learned — NACLs are powerful but easy to shoot yourself in the foot with stateless denies. thanks for fast rollback
mira: closing thread after postmortem is linked, good catch everyone
